To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Setomaa case is a successful example of how to use cultural assets for the empowerment of local people and enterprises.
cultural assets are a source of regional advantage and a resource for local businesses, and that a location ‘in the geographic periphery’, can be a resource for local business development.
the cultural identity of Setomaa is the main resource for its economic development, which in turn is the main source of its cultural identity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: (1) the role of cultural identity in regional development, (2) the role of the state in supporting regional development, (3) the role of local people in regional development.
the role of cultural identity as an instrument of regional development.
a new approach to regional development: the empowerment of local people and enterprises with strong cultural and territorial identity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cultural identity and uniqueness are not only a ‘nice to have’ but also an important ‘must have’ for a successful regional development.
cultural uniqueness is a source for new regional economy, boosted by the media driven world to present difference.
the Setomaa case shows that the ‘regional advantage’ is not a ‘natural’ phenomenon, but a social and political construction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ‘Seto case’ shows that cultural assets can be leveraged as a tool for economic development, if they are used as a source of competitive advantage.
the Setomaa case study shows that the cultural and territorial identity of a location, if well maintained, can be an asset to the economic development of the region.
cultural identity can be used as a tool for economic development and that cultural assets can be a resource for local enterprise.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the local community is a source of strength and that it should be empowered to make decisions about its future.
cultural identity, as a source for regional economic growth, is an asset which is often underestimated, but which is now becoming increasingly important.
cultural identity can be a source of economic development and a way for local enterprises to empower themselves and their region.
